lead.headline: Republicans Submit Final 635-Page CLARITY Act Ahead of Procedural Vote as UK Crypto Donations Face Potential Ban
lead.tldr: US digital asset legislation is accelerating toward a floor vote while UK lawmakers simultaneously move to restrict the very crypto-funded political influence that just delivered £72 million to Reform UK, creating a transatlantic regulatory tension worth watching.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why it matters for the quarter ahead.

top_signals.title: US Republicans send ‘final’ CLARITY Act offer to DemocratsThe 635-page revised proposal includes Trump-backed ethics provisions and comes just two days before a key procedural vote.
top_signals.summary: US Republicans have submitted a revised 635-page proposal for the CLARITY Act to Democrats. The offer includes ethics provisions and arrives ahead of a critical procedural vote regarding digital asset regulation.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The inclusion of Trump-backed ethics provisions in a 635-page final offer signals that Republicans are treating digital asset regulation as a must-pass priority, which if successful would create the first comprehensive federal framework and likely trigger a repricing of US-based crypto equity and infrastructure plays.

top_signals.title: Revolut attackers threaten daily customer data leaks
top_signals.summary: Attackers have threatened to leak customer data from Revolut on a daily basis following a security breach. The incident highlights ongoing vulnerabilities in fintech platforms that integrate traditional banking with digital asset services.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Revolut's dual breach exposure—customer data now under active daily leak threat—demonstrates that fintech-crypto hybrid platforms remain systemically underinsured against social engineering, making this a diligence red flag for any LP evaluating neobank or on-ramp exposure.

top_signals.title: Revolut says customer data exposed through fake government email29m, Revolut says customer data exposed through fake government emailPassports, selfies and financial transaction histories of some customers were revealed to a fraudster using a government agency domain.
top_signals.summary: Revolut has reported a data breach where customer information, including passports and financial histories, was exposed. The breach occurred after a fraudster impersonated a government agency via a fake email domain.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The government-impersonation vector used to extract passports and financial histories from Revolut suggests that KYC/AML infrastructure at major consumer platforms is still vulnerable to basic domain spoofing, which should concern any investor underwriting identity or compliance tooling.

top_signals.title: Symbiosis says it recovered 15 BTC after Bitcoin bridge exploit, offers attacker 20% bounty
top_signals.summary: Symbiosis has recovered 15 BTC following an exploit of its Bitcoin bridge and is offering the attacker a 20% bounty for the remaining funds. While a large amount of syBTC was minted, the actual realized losses were relatively low at approximately $336,000.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Symbiosis's 15 BTC recovery and 20% bounty offer represents a maturing incident-response playbook for bridge protocols, but the fact that $336,000 in realized losses still occurred despite this response means bridge security remains a sector where we underwrite on total value locked at risk rather than recovery rate.

top_signals.title: Crypto billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne each donate £36 million to Farage's Reform UK
top_signals.summary: Crypto billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne have each donated £36 million to the Reform UK party. Simultaneously, the UK House of Lords is reviewing legislation that could ban crypto donations and limit overseas contributions.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The £72 million crypto donation pipeline to Reform UK, now under direct legislative threat from the House of Lords, creates a live test of whether crypto wealth can convert into durable political capital or whether regulators will move faster to sever that channel.

on_the_radar.title: Big Players ravage prediction markets
on_the_radar.summary: The article discusses the influence of insiders and 'big players' within prediction markets, challenging the narrative of these platforms as democratic tools. It suggests that market outcomes may be driven by a small group of powerful actors rather than collective wisdom.

on_the_radar.title: (Sm)all banks should compete on technology, not fear it
on_the_radar.summary: The article argues that community banks must embrace digital-dollar and tokenized payment options to remain competitive. Rather than launching their own stablecoins, banks should integrate these technologies to retain customer data and treasury relationships.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin Suisse to shift up to half of Swiss jobs abroad34m
on_the_radar.summary: Bitcoin Suisse is planning to relocate up to half of its Swiss-based workforce to international locations. This move is part of a strategic shift to optimize operations and expand its global footprint.

on_the_radar.title: Hyperliquid’s biggest risk is regulation, says Ran Neuner40m
on_the_radar.summary: Analyst Ran Neuner identifies regulatory pressure as the primary risk factor for the Hyperliquid platform. The discussion focuses on the potential impact of legal scrutiny on decentralized exchanges.

on_the_radar.title: Established businesses, not startups, are driving growth in RWAs
on_the_radar.summary: The article discusses the growth of Real World Assets (RWAs) in the blockchain space, noting that established businesses are now the primary drivers of adoption over startups. This shift suggests a move toward institutional integration of tokenized assets.

on_the_radar.title: Metaplanet reverses course on executive options with 41% cut to potential shares, scraps employee warrant plan
on_the_radar.summary: Metaplanet has significantly reduced potential share issuance by cutting executive options by 41% and scrapping its employee warrant plan. These measures follow a sharp 17% decline in the company's stock price over two trading sessions.

on_the_radar.title: Robinhood’s crypto volume increases 61% in August, still down 38% YoY40m
on_the_radar.summary: Robinhood saw a 61% month-over-month increase in crypto trading volume during August. Despite this short-term growth, the volume remains 38% lower compared to the same period last year.

on_the_radar.title: Standard Chartered forecasts SKY rising fivefold to $0.325 by 20289m, Standard Chartered forecasts SKY rising fivefold to $0.325 by 2028The bank expects Sky to pass five times as much value to token holders by 2028 as USDS adoption and borrowing capacity continue to expand.
on_the_radar.summary: Standard Chartered predicts that the SKY token will see a fivefold increase in value passed to holders by 2028. This growth is expected to be driven by the expansion of USDS adoption and borrowing capacity.

worth_a_read.title: 💻 $LAPTOP Flop Shows Market's Moved on From Celeb Memecoins
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's analysis of the $LAPTOP memecoin failure provides concrete evidence that celebrity-token fatigue has reached institutional-scale, which matters for anyone still pricing consumer crypto adoption through influencer-driven token metrics.

linkedin_post:
The CLARITY Act is 635 pages now. That is not a negotiating document; that is a signal that Republicans have stopped asking whether digital asset legislation happens and started deciding whose provisions survive. The Trump-backed ethics language is the tell. This is being built to pass a floor vote, not to stall in committee.

Across the Atlantic, the same week that Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne each put £36 million into Reform UK, the House of Lords is reviewing a ban on exactly those crypto donations. Two moves, one direction: political money wants in, and regulators are scrambling to define the door.

We do not underwrite regulatory risk as binary. We underwrite it as sequencing risk—who gets clarity first, and what that clarity prices out of competing jurisdictions. The US is accelerating. The UK is hesitating. That divergence is already showing up in where early-stage founders choose to domicile.

The test: if the procedural vote this week advances CLARITY to floor debate, we will see a repricing of US exchange and custody infrastructure within 48 hours. If it stalls, the capital that moved on that signal moves back to offshore ambiguity. Either outcome is tradeable. Only one is priced.
